page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.8xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY cores operating at a base frequency of 3.1 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. This instance does not include any local storage or integrated GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Benchmark results place this instance in the average performance tier for its hardware class. The Intel Xeon processor achieves a single-core stress-ng score of 1436.68 and a multi-core score of 30666.35, supported by AVX-512 vector extensions for accelerated vector and matrix operations. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 1705.41 GB/sec, which drops to 109.89 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. In application-level tests, the instance processes 28.91 million Redis SET operations per second and delivers a static web serving throughput of 21.45 GB/sec. For lightweight machine learning tasks, it handles 135M parameter LLM prompt processing at 1539.55 tokens per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.hfg6.8xlarge offers a balanced resource density for workloads requiring dedicated CPU performance without the overhead of specialized hardware. The primary tradeoff is the complete absence of local storage and GPU accelerators, meaning storage-heavy or deep learning training tasks must rely on external network volumes. This configuration is highly suitable for multi-threaded applications, web serving, database operations, and moderate computational tasks such as software compilation and text processing.
